item.title: Brewers and Rays meet with a first World Series title guaranteed
item.description: For the first time since 1980, the World Series matches two franchises that have never won it. Milwaukee brings a club-record 103 wins and its first pennant since 1982; Tampa Bay returns after a comeback ALCS. Game 1 on Friday pairs two of MLB's smaller-market, lower-payroll clubs.

item.title: Doncic and Kessler launch the post-LeBron Lakers with a rout
item.description: Los Angeles opened its first season after LeBron James with a 127-105 win over Golden State. Luka Doncic had 28 points, eight rebounds and seven assists, while newcomer Walker Kessler scored 26 on 12-for-12 shooting as the Lakers built a 35-point lead.

item.title: 2027 Tours reward time trialists and return to Britain
item.description: The 2027 men's Tour de France will start in Edinburgh and include 71 kilometers of individual time trials, the most since 2012. The Tour de France Femmes begins in Leeds with a London team time trial and finishes atop the Puy de Dome.

item.title: England's football regulator says it can force club owners to sell
item.description: Independent Football Regulator chair David Kogan says the new body can remove owners who fail its fitness and propriety tests. It may examine Manchester City after the club's appeal over 114 Premier League financial-rule breaches, and it also wants more money flowing to lower-division clubs.

item.title: LeBron's Philadelphia debut spoils the Knicks' banner night
item.description: LeBron James began his record-extending 24th NBA season with 14 points, nine rebounds and seven assists as Philadelphia beat defending champion New York 106-100. Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 28 points, quieting Madison Square Garden after the Knicks received rings and raised their first title banner in 53 years.

item.title: Celebrini scores twice as Sharks erase two-goal deficit
item.description: Macklin Celebrini scored the opening goal and the overtime winner as San Jose rallied past Montreal 4-3. Michael Misa and Tyler Toffoli erased a 3-1 third-period deficit before Celebrini converted Ivar Stenberg's no-look pass on a power play 2:13 into overtime.

item.title: Rays finish comeback to clinch a World Series berth
item.description: After entering Sunday one win from elimination, Tampa Bay completed a three-game rally by beating Cleveland 7-3 in Game 6. Junior Caminero and Yandy Díaz hit two-run homers, while Freddy Peralta earned ALCS MVP honors. The Rays will visit Milwaukee in Friday's World Series opener.

item.title: 49ers hold off Washington to remain the NFL's lone unbeaten
item.description: San Francisco improved to 6-0 with a 23-17 win after Washington nearly erased a 23-3 deficit. Brock Purdy threw for 264 yards and a touchdown, Christian McCaffrey ran for two scores, and the 49ers stopped the Commanders' final drive to preserve their best start since 2019.

item.title: Knicks begin title defense in an NBA built to resist dynasties
item.description: New York opens its defense of a first championship in 53 years with its top five scorers back, but recent history is formidable: the NBA has crowned eight different champions in eight seasons. The opener also brings LeBron James' Philadelphia debut to Madison Square Garden after the banner ceremony.

item.title: Rays move one win from World Series behind Rasmussen
item.description: Tampa Bay beat Cleveland 3-1 in Game 5 to take a 3-2 ALCS lead, a major step beyond Sunday’s 2-2 tie. Drew Rasmussen allowed one run over seven innings, and the Rays return home needing one victory for their first World Series trip since 2020.

item.title: Texans edge Jaguars in London on last-second field goal
item.description: Ka’imi Fairbairn kicked a 49-yard field goal as time expired to give Houston a 34-31 win over Jacksonville. C.J. Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns, while Travis Hunter Jr. became the first NFL player since 2002 with a touchdown catch and an interception in the same game.

item.title: Manchester City stays perfect as Haaland reaches a milestone
item.description: Manchester City beat Ipswich 3-2 for a seventh win in seven Premier League matches. Erling Haaland scored twice, becoming the fastest player to 100 non-penalty league goals, but limped off late and left City waiting on his fitness.

item.title: Rays even ALCS at 2-2 behind Aranda's three-hit night
item.description: Jonathan Aranda collected three hits, drove in two runs and scored the go-ahead run as Tampa Bay beat Cleveland 7-3. The Rays erased a 2-1 series deficit, guaranteeing the American League Championship Series will return to St. Petersburg for Game 6.

item.title: Auburn topples No. 1 Georgia on a wild day of upsets
item.description: Alex McPherson's 34-yard field goal at the horn gave Auburn a 27-24 win at Georgia, its first victory in Athens in 21 years. No. 2 Notre Dame, No. 5 Indiana, No. 6 Alabama and No. 7 Texas also lost in a Saturday that scrambled the college football race.

item.title: WNBA reaches new heights as Engelbert's tenure winds down
item.description: Outgoing commissioner Cathy Engelbert said the WNBA drew more than 90 million U.S. viewers, 3.8 million spectators and 51 million-viewer telecasts this season. The Finals between Golden State and Atlanta will produce a first-time champion.
